Model code files are moved from `contente/models` to `content/models/stan`.

This change makes it easier to add implementation specific model info files.

author: Eero Linna <eero.linna@gmail.com>
message:
python: Remove dispatch methods from Posterior

This removes the methods from Posterior that dispatch to methods of Model or
Data.

So now for example `posterior.model_code("stan")` is written
`posterior.model.code("stan")`, so the new code calls the `code` method on `Model`
instead of `model_code` on `Posterior`.

The aim of this change is to make the library more simple. This change aligns
well with the Zen of Python guideline "There should be one-- and preferably only one
--obvious way to do it.".

Of course if having two ways of doing something adds value then it can be worth
the duplication, however in this case I don't really see a big difference
between `posterior.model_code("stan")` and `posterior.model.code("stan")`.

author: Eero Linna <eero.linna@gmail.com>
message:
Add model implementations to the API

Add method `implementations` to Model, which takes a framework name and returns
a model implementation object for that framework

Currently model implementation objects only have `load` method. Calling it loads
the underlying model of the framework being used

Here's an example how this might be used.

```python
from posteriordb import PosteriorDatabase
my_pdb = PosteriorDatabase("../posterior_database/") # replace path if needed
model=my_pdb.model("eight_schools_centered")
data = my_pdb.data("eight_schools")
```

We can load a Stan model and obtain posterior draws

```python
stan_imp = model.implementation("stan")
stan_model = stan_imp.load()
stan_draws = stan_model.sampling(data=data.values())
```

We can do the same with a PyMC3 model

```python
import pymc3
pymc_imp = model.implementation("pymc3")
get_pymc_model = pymc_imp.load()
pymc_model = get_pymc_model(data.values())
pymc_draws = pymc3.sampling.sample(model=pymc_model)
```

Further down the line we might want to also add other methods to the model
implementation objects. Obtaining prior or predictive draws might be one of
these potential new methods.

message:
Preparations for using remote posterior databases in python

This moves all filesystem related logic to the PosteriorDatabase class. Later we
can add a CachingRemotePosteriorDatabase that downloads the files from the
remote posterior database (for example a github repo) and caches them locally.
Then we can add a convenience function that creates a local posterior db if
passed a local filepath and a remote posterior db if passed an url, and if
passed nothing it can default to our github repository.

author: Ben <bbh@umich.edu>
message:
Update R/makedist.R

Revised two warning messages in makedist.R, both arising in scenarios where user has asked match_on to compute a large number of distances.  They aim to head off two misinterpretations:
1.  either warning might suggest to the user that the matching problem is too large for match_on, as opposed to for fullmatch/pairmatch etc.  Larger distances can take a while to compute, during which the user sits looking at this warning message; she might mistakenly conclude that she's done something to impede match_on, and conclude the software has hit a dead end.  We need to reword to limit this suggestion; here is one possibility.
2. The second of the revised warnings, the warning about large problems that's issued when the user has provided a within argument, may be thrown when the user is moving toward a small enough problem for fullmatch/pairmatch etc, but isn't quite there yet.  Example:

md.hosp <- exactMatch(pr_vcd ~ hosp.code, data=psdata)
md.tmp <- match_on(pr_vcd ~PS.glmer, within=md.hosp, data=pscores)
md.tmp <- match_on(md.tmp, within=caliper(md.tmp, width=.05) )


In these cases it would be nice to avoid suggesting to the user that she's not using match_on correctly, and in general to avoid needlessly alarming her.  Again, open to other ways of doing this.

author: Hansen <bbh@umich.edu>
message:
Revert "Pass disthash+hint down call stack from fullmatch.matrix()"

(The idea of passing down the combination of the disthash and the hint
was to use them to inform decisions at the subproblem level as to whether
a new attempt at solving the problem needs to be made, vs whether the
last one was good enough.   But along the way I realized that it's likely
to be expensive to inspect the hint info to decide if the problem that
had been solved was similar in relevant respects. It seems a more promising
approach to design and implement these checks inside of update.fullmatch()/
update.pairmatch() etc, probably at the problem rather than the subproblem
level.)

This reverts commit 4dbf103860c122764b65d830f6305064f0d4c9e5.

author: Ben Hansen <bbh@umich.edu>
message:
Remove "How closely did I match?" subsec

We were recommending the use of `summary.optmatch()`
to assemble matched distance info, but as of this writing
it doesn't do that, and the subsection is internally incoherent
(promises matched distance information that the command we present
does not return). We may reenable that when addressing #173,
at which time we should consider reverting this commit.

If on the other hand we resolve #173 without restoring
sum-of-matched-distances information to the output of
`summary.optmatch()`, then it becomes more important to add
vignette material explaining how to use `matched.distances()`
to extract this info.  Cf. #185.

Distributions are free to put the headers in non-standard locations as
long as the R_INCLUDE_DIR variable is properly set to point to the
location. Normally, this is identical to R_HOME/include, but in the case
of ArchLinux, the location is /usr/include/R. The makefile.linux should
now be more flexible.

vector for each item in the treatment vector. A smarter algorithm would
pre-sort the vectors, and then iterate over them with a "sliding window"
to count the number of controls within a certain distance from the
treated unit.

author: Ben B Hansen <bbh@umich.edu>
message:
hasty solution to malformed error message

This fixes an issue due to long x'es being split into
multiple entries in a character vector. As an example,
an x of this form was fed to fullmatch
    psDist2+caliper(psDist2,4)
    +caliper(absdist,2)
    +caliper(mahalDist,40)
(This input was mistaken b/c `psDist2` did not exist.)
The error message that was generated read
    Error in value[[3L]](cond): Can't find psDist2 + caliper(psDist2, 4) + caliper(absdist, 2) + caliper(mahalDist, . If it lives within the data frame provided
    as the data argument, try
    meddat$psDist2 + caliper(psDist2, 4) + caliper(absdist, 2) + caliper(mahalDist,
    Can't find   40).
    If it lives within the data frame
    provided as the data argument, try meddat$    40)

which doesn't make sense due to x_str being a character vector of length 2,
with the final "`40)`" having wrapped to its second entry.

author: Ben B. Hansen <bbh@umich.edu>
message:
Require nodes to have unique `name`s, at least within levels of `groups`

(Presently the requirement is only checked when inspecting single `groups`
NodeInfo's, to avoid slowdowns when combining NodeInfo's.  Not that I checked
that any slowdowns really would result from this; perhaps it would be very fast
to execute something along lines of `anyDuplicated(paste(groups, name))`.
Benchmarks presented in this post suggest base::duplicated() should be
fast with moderate-sized data frames, which NodeInfo's will be:
  https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47539860/r-remove-duplicates-from-a-dataframe-based-on-categories-in-a-column
.)

message:
Address scores() mishandling of svyglm's

svyglm's leave a '(weights)' column in their model.frame's even
if not invoked with a weights= argument; they typically receive
weights through their `design=` argument.

To me it seemed probably safest in general to
look to `object`'s original call to decide whether or
not an explicit weights argument is appropriate. This this commit.

author: Josh Buckner <bucknerj@umich.edu>
message:
Use meaningful group names in dbind()

When a named list of ISMs is passed to dbind(), use the list names as
group levels in the resulting BISM. When BISMs are in the mix, preserve
their existing @groups levels. Unnamed entries fall back to position-based
numeric indices, skipping any that collide with existing labels.

message:
Add cellIRMI and cellM imputation functions for mixed data

Two exported functions:
- imputeCellIRMI(): flagship cellwise-robust IRMI for mixed data
  (continuous via cellIRWLS + categorical via weighted multinom)
- imputeCellM(): lightweight single-formula cell-weighted M-estimation

Five internal helpers for design matrix construction, cell weight
expansion, uncertainty propagation, and predictive mean matching.

775 lines. Uses cellIRWLS engine from cellwise_utils.R.

author: Matthias Templ <matthias.templ@gmail.com>
message:
Add cell-weighted IRWLS engine for cellwise-robust imputation

Core building blocks for cellwise-robust imputation (Topic A):
- cellWeights(): per-cell contamination weights for mixed data
- cellWeightsFromResiduals(): psi-weights from regression residuals
- cellIRWLS(): cell-weighted IRWLS with per-cell design matrix weighting
  (NOT min() row-collapse — each cell gets its own weight)
- huber_weight(), tukey_weight(): robust weight functions
- .weighted_qr_solve(): numerically stable QR-based solver

376 lines, 8 functions, all with roxygen2 documentation.

author: Matthias Templ <matthias.templ@gmail.com>
message:
Add cellEM: EM with latent contamination indicators for mixed data

imputeCellEM(): cellwise-robust EM imputation with:
- Latent binary indicators (clean vs contaminated) per continuous cell
- E-step: posterior clean probabilities, conditional mean/variance per variable
- M-step: pairwise cell-weighted covariance (w_ij * w_ik, NOT min() collapse)
- Categorical variables via weighted multinomial with geometric mean weights
- Robust initialization via Gnanadesikan-Kettenring
- Guards: Sigma regularization, epsilon/gamma clamping, eigenvalue clamping

877 lines. Distinct from cellGMM: single clean component, mixed data support.

message:
use has_*() for pkgdown reference index

add a @family tag to group functions in the
reference index for pkgdown
(https://statistikat.github.io/VIM/reference/index.html).

This is done with the has_concept() selector
in pkgdown/_pkgdown.yaml. As a side effect,
the reference pages are now cross linked in
the R documentation viewer as well as on pkgdown.

The new families are named like the groups
used in the reference index.
* plotting functions
* imputation methods

Also use the has_keyword() selector to
automatically group all datasets into a category.

has_keyword() was introduced recently in
https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdown/pull/1241.
Therefore, the development version of pkgdown is
now necessary in order to render the
pkgdown-docs for VIM.

author: Matthias Templ <matthias.templ@gmail.com>
message:
Add cellEM: EM with latent contamination indicators for mixed data

imputeCellEM(): cellwise-robust EM imputation with:
- Latent binary indicators (clean vs contaminated) per continuous cell
- E-step: posterior clean probabilities, conditional mean/variance per variable
- M-step: pairwise cell-weighted covariance (w_ij * w_ik, NOT min() collapse)
- Categorical variables via weighted multinomial with geometric mean weights
- Robust initialization via Gnanadesikan-Kettenring
- Guards: Sigma regularization, epsilon/gamma clamping, eigenvalue clamping

877 lines. Distinct from cellGMM: single clean component, mixed data support.

author: Matthias Templ <matthias.templ@gmail.com>
message:
Add cell-weighted IRWLS engine for cellwise-robust imputation

Core building blocks for cellwise-robust imputation (Topic A):
- cellWeights(): per-cell contamination weights for mixed data
- cellWeightsFromResiduals(): psi-weights from regression residuals
- cellIRWLS(): cell-weighted IRWLS with per-cell design matrix weighting
  (NOT min() row-collapse — each cell gets its own weight)
- huber_weight(), tukey_weight(): robust weight functions
- .weighted_qr_solve(): numerically stable QR-based solver

376 lines, 8 functions, all with roxygen2 documentation.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
fix(cmake): Handle Double CMake in Using Projects

A typical "ExperimentRoot" project uses FairRoot by using
its find-Module (by adding the right path) and calling
find_package(FairRoot).

This setup worked for the first call to CMake (configure
step), but reconfiguring (running CMake again) did not
work correctly.

Add tests for this (that fail without this fix).

The find module recursively calls find_package(FairRoot
CONFIG) to load the new config mode package.
This sets FairRoot_DIR to the directory containing the
config mode package. This variable is a cache variable and
persists into the next run of CMake.

The old find module used to think, that FairRoot_DIR could
be the prefix of the FairRoot installation.

Rewrite:

* Use FAIRROOTPATH and ENV{FAIRROOTPATH} only to extend
  CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH to search the config mode package
* Use FairRoot_PREFIX from the config mode package to guide
  further old style detection
* Use FindPackageHandleStandardArgs

author: Florian Uhlig <f.uhlig@gsi.de>
message:
Store correct random seed in parameter container

Between Root 6.22 and 6.24 the return value of TRandom3::GetSeed() was changed.
Since Root 6.24 the function GetSeed returns the current element of the state
used to generate the random number which returns a fixed value of 624 for
TRandom3.
To get the seed value which was set by the function SetSeed one neeeds to use
the GetSeed() function from the base class (gRandom->TRandom::GetSeed()),

FairSoft apr21p2 does not have the problem but any later FairSoft version will
save the wrong information in the parameter container FairBaseParSet
irrespective of the seed value defined in Root.
This commit fixes the issue and saves the correct seed value specified by
gRandom->SetSeed(<your value>).

(cherry picked from commit 20d04315fbd85c16ab39a05aaaacbfc75aadd10b)

author: shahoian <ruben.shahoyan@cern.ch>
message:
Ask FairRunSim if TGeo should be imported to VMC

FairMCApplication.cxx unconditionally calls TVirtualMC::GetMC()->SetRootGeometry()
Materials/Media created via VMC are added both to TGeo and VMC geometry, so that
the importing the TGeo to VMC in the e.g. TGeant3TGeo::FinishGeometry() leads to
materials duplication and the loss of special (e.g. optical) properties set directly
on VMC materials 1st copy. This patch introduces a flag in the AliRunSim, which tells
to FairMCApplication if the TGeo should be imported to VMC. The flag is set to TRUE
in the constructor, therefore default behaviour of FairRoot is not altered. Those
applications which do not importing of TGeo (e.g. O2 always created the geometry
for the simulation on the fly) can set FairRunSim::SetImportTGeoToVMC(false)
BEFORE building the geometry

author: Radoslaw Karabowicz <r.karabowicz@gsi.de>
message:
fix(sim): Clarify behaviour for same-name sensitive volumes

The transport engines allow registering of multiple nodes
with the same volume/same volume name (copy mechanism).
In `FairRoot` this mechanism works provided unique volume name
over the whole geometry setup of different detectors.

The commit clarifies the situtation:
1. for same volume names in one detector, it quenches the log message
by moving `LOG` and changing it severity
from `LOG(error)` in `FairVolumeList::addVolume()`
to `LOG(debug)` in `FairModule::AddSensitiveVolume()`.
2. for same volume names accross different detectors,
the program prints appropriate `LOG(fatal)`.

Fixes the issue #1595.

base class is actually a class from boost or from stl. Switch of the compiler flag for the problematic parts of the code
using preprocessor statements. There are also such preprocessor guards for code which creates many warnings when

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Drop load_all_libs test

This test used to check `gSystem->Load()` on all installed
libraries.

1. `gSystem->Load()` is not any longer a public API, that
   FairRoot needs to support. rootmap has basically
   replaced it.
2. Loading each library alone can be a way to check,
   whether all link dependencies are properly declared.
   The linker can do that much better at build time.
   See the previous commit.
3. The current test was always succeeding.

message:
build!: Retire `BUILD_UNITTESTS` CMake switch

Technically, this is a breaking change, but this build switch did not
have any meaningful nor maintained unit tests, so we can remove it
without replacement.

Future unit tests shall be steerable via the standard CMake switch
`BUILD_TESTING` defined by the CTest module, see
https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/module/CTest.html.

Effectively, this commit also removes FairRoot's (unused) dependency on
Googletest.

author: Dennis Klein <d.klein@gsi.de>
message:
build: Workaround FindProtobuf lacking support for Protobuf >= 22

1. If we can find a Protobuf with a CMake pkg, we are good.
2. Otherwise fall back to FindProtobuf.
3. If we find Protobuf >= 22 and do not detect the missing `absl::`
   target (this is a guess that `absl::` targets will exist once
   FindProtobuf supports Protobuf >= 22), we set Protobuf as NOTFOUND.

Side notes:
Old CMake versions (< 3.27) see Protobuf >= 21 as major version 4.21+.

See also:
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v22.0
* https://protobuf.dev/news/2022-05-06/#versioning
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/12292
* https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/24847

author: Florian Uhlig <f.uhlig@gsi.de>
message:
Improve performance when using many parameters

Previously the parameters were stored in a TList. While this is okay for a
small number of entries which are accessed by the function FindObject with
the name of the object as argument this be becomes very slow when the list
is large. Since for each entry of the list a search has to be performed
this is time consuming when the list is long.
To improve the performance a more suitable data structure (THashTable)
was choosed to speed up the searching. The new data strcuture speeds up
the initilization a CBM parameter container with roughly 101000 parameters
by a factor of 5 from 145s to 27s.
Since it is unavoidable to remove the searching it becomes obvious to
limit the number of parameters in a parameter container to a small number.

message:
FairMQ: Extend Multipart and messaging API

 - Extend the multipart API to allow sending vectors of messages or helper
   thin wrapper FairMQParts. See example in examples/MQ/8-multipart.
 - NewMessage() can be used in devices instead of
   fTransportFactory->CreateMessage().
   Possible arguments remain unchanged (no args, size or data+size).
 - Send()/Receive() methods can be used in devices instead of
   fChannels.at("chan").at(i).Send()/Receive():
   Send(msg, "chan", i = 0), Receive(msg, "chan", i = 0).
 - Use the new methods in MQ examples and tests.
 - No breaking changes, but FAIRMQ_INTERFACE_VERSION is incremented to 3
   to allow to check for new methods.

author: Radoslaw Karabowicz <r.karabowicz@gsi.de>
message:
FastSimulation.

Implemented feature allows user to move transported particles
in TGeant3 or TGeant4 to any position.
It is used when implementing fast simulation in some detector
to move particle forward out of this detector to reduce computing time.

Introduced methods of the FairGenericStack should be implemened
by individual experiments, as shown in FairStack:
FastSimMoveParticleTo(): moves the particle to a position and momentum specified by the user.
FastSimStopParticle(): kill the current particle.
FastSimGetMovedIndex(): to get the stack index of the moved particle.
FastSimClearMovedIndex(): to clear the index (set it to -2).

base/sim/fastsim develops a fast simulation model for Geant4 that uses
TG4VUserFastSimulation to implement the functionality.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Convert Some Member Variables to Local Ones

On some classes, a few member variables are only really used
in one (or two) methods to handle local data. So convert
those member variables to local ones in that method.

This improves readability and locality of the code.
It also shrinks the instance's size.

Several FairMQ fixes and improvements:

- FairMQChannel: improve address validation for channels.
- FairMQChannel: add ExpectsAnotherPart() method to check if another msg part is expected (old approach still works).
- FairMQ: remove invalid transition from the run files.
- FairMQFileSink: disable ROOT termination signal handler.

author: Giulio Eulisse <giulio.eulisse@cern.ch>
message:
Remove unneeded if when deleting NULL / 0 / nullptr

C++ standard dictates that NULL / 0 / nullptr is a valid argument for
delete which then simply has no effect:

"The value of the first argument supplied to a deallocation function may
be a null pointer value; if so, and if the deallocation function is one
supplied in the standard library, the call has no effect."

I therefore think in these particular case it's safe to remove the ifs.

author: Florian Uhlig <f.uhlig@gsi.de>
message:
Store correct random seed in parameter container

Between Root 6.22 and 6.24 the return value of TRandom3::GetSeed() was changed.
Since Root 6.24 the function GetSeed returns the current element of the state
used to generate the random number which returns a fixed value of 624 for
TRandom3.
To get the seed value which was set by the function SetSeed one neeeds to use
the GetSeed() function from the base class (gRandom->TRandom::GetSeed()),

FairSoft apr21p2 does not have the problem but any later FairSoft version will
save the wrong information in the parameter container FairBaseParSet
irrespective of the seed value defined in Root.
This commit fixes the issue and saves the correct seed value specified by
gRandom->SetSeed(<your value>).

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
fix: Handle Sink/Source ownership more properly

FairRootManager and FairRun both used to `delete` fSink and
fSource. In specific situations (FairRootManager getting
destructed before FairRun) this leads to a double delete!

Deprecate the old FairRootManager::Set{Source,Sink} APIs
that take something like an owning pointer.

FairRootManager should only have a non-owning reference to
sink and source.  To allow FairRun to set it, `friend` it
from FairRootManager.

See: https://github.com/FairRootGroup/FairRoot/issues/1418
     (see "Double deleting of file source in
     FairRootManager and FairRun")

author: Alexey Rybalchenko <alexryba@gmail.com>
message:
Remove compile time transport interface switch

- Remove the compile time check of the transport implementation.
  The transport (zeromq/nanomsg) can be chosen at run time with:
  `device.SetTransport("zeromq"); // possible values are "zeromq" and "nanomsg"`.

  For devices that use FairMQProgOptions, the transport can be configured via cmd option:
  `--transport zeromq` or `--transport nanomsg`. Default values is "zeromq".
  The device receives the configured value with:
  `device.SetTransport(config.GetValue<std::string>("transport"));`

  Old method of setting transport still works. But the NANOMSG constant is not defined.

- Remove old `fairmq/prototest` directory. It was only used as a test for protobuf.
  The protobuf part of Tutorial3 does the same (with different values).

- Fix a bug in FairMQPollerNN, where the `revents` value was not initialized.
  This caused the `poller->CheckOutput()` to trigger when it should not.

author: Dennis Klein <d.klein@gsi.de>
message:
build: Workaround FindProtobuf lacking support for Protobuf >= 22

1. If we can find a Protobuf with a CMake pkg, we are good.
2. Otherwise fall back to FindProtobuf.
3. If we find Protobuf >= 22 and do not detect the missing `absl::`
   target (this is a guess that `absl::` targets will exist once
   FindProtobuf supports Protobuf >= 22), we set Protobuf as NOTFOUND.

Side notes:
Old CMake versions (< 3.27) see Protobuf >= 21 as major version 4.21+.

See also:
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v22.0
* https://protobuf.dev/news/2022-05-06/#versioning
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/12292
* https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/24847

author: Radoslaw Karabowicz <r.karabowicz@gsi.de>
message:
fix(sim): Clarify behaviour for same-name sensitive volumes

The transport engines allow registering of multiple nodes
with the same volume/same volume name (copy mechanism).
In `FairRoot` this mechanism works provided unique volume name
over the whole geometry setup of different detectors.

The commit clarifies the situtation:
1. for same volume names in one detector, it quenches the log message
by moving `LOG` and changing it severity
from `LOG(error)` in `FairVolumeList::addVolume()`
to `LOG(debug)` in `FairModule::AddSensitiveVolume()`.
2. for same volume names accross different detectors,
the program prints appropriate `LOG(fatal)`.

Fixes the issue #1595.

message:
FairMQ: Extend Multipart and messaging API

 - Extend the multipart API to allow sending vectors of messages or helper
   thin wrapper FairMQParts. See example in examples/MQ/8-multipart.

 - NewMessage() can be used in devices instead of
   fTransportFactory->CreateMessage().
   Possible arguments remain unchanged (no args, size or data+size).

 - Send()/Receive() methods can be used in devices instead of
   fChannels.at("chan").at(i).Send()/Receive()`:
   Send(msg, "chan", i = 0), Receive(msg, "chan", i = 0).

 - Use the new methods in MQ examples and tests.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Be more Pedantic During Linking

On Linux, when creating a shared library, it is usually
allowed to have undefined symbols.
One reason, why this might be useful: A "main" program that
links to the library provides that symbol.

None of the shared libraries in FairRoot use this feature.
So let the linker enforce this.
Undefined symbols will now result in an error.

author: Florian Uhlig <F.Uhlig@gsi.de>
message:
Complete rewrite of the file handling of the input files. All functionality has moved from FairRunAna
to FairRootManager. All input files are added to the input chain during initialization of the Run. During
this step it is also checked that all input files have the same branch structure. If not the execution
is stopped. After creation of the input tree all friend trees are created. To do this the branch structure
of the friend files are checked and files with the same branch structure are added to the same friend chain.
Before adding the friend chains to the input chain it is checked that all chains have the same runids in the
same order and that all runids hold the same number of events. In case there is somewhere a mismatch the
execution of the macro is stopped.

Start to use the new FairLogger.

Add extensive comments to the new functionality.

Since some functions of FairRunAna have disappeared two files in the eventdisplay directory had to be changed
accordingly.

author: Florian Uhlig <f.uhlig@gsi.de>
message:
Improve performance when using many parameters

Previously the parameters were stored in a TList. While this is okay for a
small number of entries which are accessed by the function FindObject with
the name of the object as argument this be becomes very slow when the list
is large. Since for each entry of the list a search has to be performed
this is time consuming when the list is long.
To improve the performance a more suitable data structure (THashTable)
was choosed to speed up the searching. The new data strcuture speeds up
the initilization a CBM parameter container with roughly 101000 parameters
by a factor of 5 from 145s to 27s.
Since it is unavoidable to remove the searching it becomes obvious to
limit the number of parameters in a parameter container to a small number.

So we need to delete our TTree before closing or
destructing the TFile.

author: Radoslaw Karabowicz <r.karabowicz@gsi.de>
message:
fix(sim): Clarify behaviour for same-name sensitive volumes

The transport engines allow registering of multiple nodes
with the same volume/same volume name (copy mechanism).
In `FairRoot` this mechanism works provided unique volume name
over the whole geometry setup of different detectors.

The commit clarifies the situtation:
1. for same volume names in one detector, it quenches the log message
by moving `LOG` and changing it severity
from `LOG(error)` in `FairVolumeList::addVolume()`
to `LOG(debug)` in `FairModule::AddSensitiveVolume()`.
2. for same volume names accross different detectors,
it crashes the program with appropriate `LOG(fatal)`.

Fixes the issue #1595.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
fix: First set of TFile::Get Related leaks

It turned out that `TFile::Get<>` returns an owning
pointer.  So store this into a unique_ptr as soon as
possible, so that the memory is handled correctly.

If one stores a TList in a root file, it is best to mark it
as an owning TList (if it is), so that readers do not have
to explicitly `->Delete()` the contents of the TList.

This fixes a first set of instances.

See: https://root-forum.cern.ch/t/solved-memory-leak-with-tfile-get/19683/8

message:
ROOT test script did not take into account externally defined LD_LIBRARY_PATH

detail: test scripts generated from ROOT macros (such as examples/simulation/Tutorial1/macros)
        set an LD_LIBRARY_PATH which is not complete. In particular it does not pick up any external
        LD_LIBRARY_PATH to my compiler (which in this case resides somewhere on the afs) but just
        overwrites it.

        This patch provides a workaround by augmenting the tests LD_LIBRARY_PATH with the externally
        user-defined LD_LIBRARY_PATH. An alternative solution might be to fix the generated
        LD_LIBRARY_PATH which should take into account the compiler/libc paths
        (as it does in PATH by the way).

author: Florian Uhlig <f.uhlig@gsi.de>
message:
build: Modernize `YAMLCPPLIB` variable with *target alias*

Since CMake 3.18 we can use the more expressive and more strictly typed target alias
instead of having a simple variable that just contains an untyped string. This commit
modernizes the variable by creating a local target alias if the new target name is not
defined. The alias is local because CMake resolves it during target export. This means
users of an exported FairRoot target will not see our alias name and will **not** need
any name switching logic on their end for the purpose of using any FairRoot library
depending on yaml-cpp.

author: Sebastien Binet <binet@cern.ch>
message:
examples/advanced: cmake support for go-examples

This CL adds basic support for compiling the Go-based examples.
Go is quite opinionated wrt a project layout.
It needs an environment variable $GOPATH (not unlike $PYTHONPATH)
pointing at a directory, under which a 'src' directory will hold all
the sources:
 $> cd $GOPATH
 $> ls
 src bin pkg
 $> tree -L 4 src
 src
 └── github.com
     ├── go-mangos
     │   └── mangos
     │       ├── AUTHORS
     │       ├── compat
     │       ├── conn.go
     │       ├── core.go
     │       ├── ...
     │       ├── util.go
     │       └── waiter.go
     └── sbinet-alice
         └── go-ex-sink-mq

This allows to have:
 $> go get github.com/sbinet-alice/go-ex-sink-mq

- fetch the sources from github.com/sbinet-alice/go-ex-sink-mq
- retrieve the dependencies of that program
  (github.com/go-mangos/mangos/...)
- compile all libraries under $GOPATH/pkg
- compile and install programs under $GOPATH/bin

To integrate with CMake:
- put the sources of go-processor and go-sink under
  `advanced/GoTutorial/src`
- make GOPATH point at advanced/GoTutorial
- use $GOBIN to make `go get` install the program(s) under that
  directory instead of $GOPATH/bin (which would be against CMake
  out-of-tree-build policy)

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Use WriteTObject instead of cd + Write

Instead of
```c++
tfile->cd();
tobj->Write();
```
one can also do
```c++
tfile->WriteTObject(tobj);
```

This has the advantage that it does not modify the global
gDirectory/gFile (which the calling code might want to keep).

Also fix some small memory leaks.

See-Also: https://root.cern/root/htmldoc/guides/users-guide/InputOutput.html#saving-objects-to-disk

author: Dennis Klein <d.klein@gsi.de>
message:
build: Workaround FindProtobuf lacking support for Protobuf >= 22

1. If we can find a Protobuf with a CMake pkg, we are good.
2. Otherwise fall back to FindProtobuf.
3. If we find Protobuf >= 22 and do not detect the missing `absl::`
   target (this is a guess that `absl::` targets will exist once
   FindProtobuf supports Protobuf >= 22), we set Protobuf as NOTFOUND.

Side notes:
Old CMake versions (< 3.27) see Protobuf >= 21 as major version 4.21+.

See also:
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v22.0
* https://protobuf.dev/news/2022-05-06/#versioning
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/12292
* https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/24847

author: mkrzewic <mikolaj.krzewicki@cern.ch>
message:
Support multiple endpoints per socket

Sent messages will be scheduled among the endpoints according to socket
type: PUB will send the same data to all endpoints simultaneously, PUSH
will do round robin transfer.
Incoming data is fair queued between endpoints.

This is a feature of at least zeromq and nanomsg.

_____________
To use: in the device configuration, instead of specifying just one address,
specify a comma separated list e.g.

tcp://localhost:123,ipc:///tmp/socket

the connection method (bind/connect) applies to all endpoints in this case.
______________
Mixing binding and connecting endpoints is supported:
prefix "@" means "bind", "+" (or ">") means connect, e.g.

+tcp://localhost:123,@ipc:///tmp/socket,ipc:///tmp/asd

(in case of missing prefix, the default channel method is used for that
endpoint).

author: Florian Uhlig <f.uhlig@gsi.de>
message:
Improve performance when using many parameters

Previously the parameters were stored in a TList. While this is okay for a
small number of entries which are accessed by the function FindObject with
the name of the object as argument this be becomes very slow when the list
is large. Since for each entry of the list a search has to be performed
this is time consuming when the list is long.
To improve the performance a more suitable data structure (THashTable)
was choosed to speed up the searching. The new data strcuture speeds up
the initilization a CBM parameter container with roughly 101000 parameters
by a factor of 5 from 145s to 27s.
Since it is unavoidable to remove the searching it becomes obvious to
limit the number of parameters in a parameter container to a small number.

Two tests available, in pure MQ and in DDS.

message:
feat(sim): Allow branch registration in `FairGenerator`

Introduced new function `FairMCApplication::InitFinalizer()`
which initializes event generator, tasks, and triggers
`FairRootManager::WriteFolder()` function.
This new function is called from `InitMC()`
and from `InitOnWorker()` for TGeant4 MT mode.

Previously the funcionality of `InitFinalizer` was
split between `InitGeometry()` and `AddIons()`, which caused
problems because
TGeant3 calls `AddIons()` first, `InitGeometry()` second,
TGeant4 calls `InitGeometry()` first, `AddIons()` second.

Current implementation assures that initialization of
event generators and tasks come before `WriteFolder`.

Fixes issues #1183 and #1567.

message:
Improve CXX_STANDARD Detection

First for users of FairRoot:
* FairRoot exports the `CXX_STANDARD` level as
  `FairRoot_CXX_STANDARD`.
* `Check_Compiler()` uses this to set the minimum
  `CXX_STANDARD` for any users of FairRoot.  You should
  call `Check_Compiler()` after `find_package(FairRoot)`.

For FairRoot itself:
* If `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD` is not set from outside, detect
  ROOT's `CXX_STANDARD` from its
  `target_compile_features()`.  This means, that
  `Check_Compiler()` must be called after
  `find_package(ROOT)`.
* If `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD` is not set, try to ask
  fairsoft-config.
* Handle `PROJECT_MIN_CXX_STANDARD`.

message:
docs(doxygen): Declutter Sidebar (Modules)

The left sidebar of the Doxygen docs has a lot of entries.

A number of them are related to directories with only C++
code in them.  Many of them represent public/exported CMake
targets.

Doxygen has a structural element called "Modules" (in the
sidebar) to put those things under.  Modules can even have

author: Dennis Klein <d.klein@gsi.de>
message:
FairMQ: Parameterize the command interface initializing with sub socket

! THIS PATCH BREAKS NANOMSG TRANSPORT !

The subscriber command socket was created using the transport factory of
the channel which might not implement sub sockets. This patch creates
the subscriber command sockets in the device initialization and passes
them down (move) to the command interface initialization.

This patch puts more focus on the GetSocket interface of FairMQSocket,
because all command sockets are now implemented with the default
transport - the channels use an internal poller which polls over sockets
of potentially different transports now (e.g. zeromq command socket and
nanomsg data socket). Basically, all transports need to return file
descriptors compatible to be used in a single poll set. THIS IS NOT THE CASE!

! THIS PATCH BREAKS NANOMSG TRANSPORT !

message:
Improve adding container to the container factory

Add a function to add a container to the factory that also checks if the
container already exist. If the container already exist it is not added
again and kFALSE is returned. Otherwise it is added and kTRUE is returned.
The "normal" way to add containers is to use the TList data member directly
which will not report any errors when adding the container. Only when the
destructor of the runtime database is called one will see an error message

Error in <TList::Delete>: A list is accessing an object (0x55d2e2220550)
already deleted (list name = TList)

step), but reconfiguring (running CMake again) did not
work correctly.

Add tests for this (that fail without this fix).

The find module recursively calls find_package(FairRoot
CONFIG) to load the new config mode package.
This sets FairRoot_DIR to the directory containing the
config mode package. This variable is a cache variable and
persists into the next run of CMake.

The old find module used to think, that FairRoot_DIR could
be the prefix of the FairRoot installation.

Rewrite:

* Use FAIRROOTPATH and ENV{FAIRROOTPATH} only to extend
  CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH to search the config mode package
* Use FairRoot_PREFIX from the config mode package to guide
  further old style detection
* Use FindPackageHandleStandardArgs

fix: First set of TFile::Get Related leaks

It turned out that `TFile::Get<>` returns an owning
pointer.  So store this into a unique_ptr as soon as
possible, so that the memory is handled correctly.

If one stores a TList in a root file, it is best to mark it
as an owning TList (if it is), so that readers do not have
to explicitly `->Delete()` the contents of the TList.

This fixes a first set of instances.

author: Sandro Wenzel <sandro.wenzel@cern.ch>
message:
Add consistency check/warning in FairMCApplication::ConstructGeometry

The FairMCApplication::ConstructGeometry assumes that the geometry volumes
are fully instantiated after calling the ConstructGeometry function on each detector modules.

This might not be the case, for instance when users are using TVirtualMC::Gsvol interface with
negative parameters which get fixed only later (during the closing phase of the geometry).
In consequence, all lookup tables might be incomplete or inconsistent.

This commit provides the following:

 * Issue a warning when ConstructGeometry was actually incomplete

 * Checking if gGeoManager is available at beginning of function

 * Fixing a size problem in a for-loop used for the index to module mapping

author: Radoslaw Karabowicz <r.karabowicz@gsi.de>
message:
fix(sim): Remove `WriteFolder` from `FairMCApplication::InitGeometry`

The function `WriteFolder` (since the introduction of the `MTMode`)
was misused to remove the `TFolder` from `gROOT`
after it was used to create the output tree.
Purely for that reason `WriteFolder` was called in the `InitGeometry()`.
This folder is no longer removed in the sink's `WriteFolder()`.

Introduced a new `FairRootManager::RemoveOutputFolderForMtMode()` function
which removes the `TFolder` from `gROOT`, which is needed in the
MT mode in TGeant4 transport.
Used this function in `FairMCApplicaiton::InitGeometry()`
and in `FairMCApplication::InitFinalizer()`.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
FairRun: Now Owns the FairSource

FairRunAna and FairRunOnline both had a SetSource method.
Both used to just call SetSource on FairRootManager.
Move this into FairRun.

FairRootManager deletes the source in its destructor. As
FairRootManager is a singleton, this happens very late in
the process lifetime. Too late for some ROOT interpreter
use cases.
So move the ownership to FairRun.
FairRun makes sure that FairRootManager does not have a
pointer to delete.

message:
Fix a runtime error with newer XCode versions

When using boost/program_options in a header file the generated dictinonary
can't be loaded at runtime and the macro crashes.
Don't use boost in the header file such that there is no problem when using

the underlying problem is obviously in the libc++ shipped by Apple.
(see https://github.com/root-project/root/issues/12762)

author: Florian Uhlig <f.uhlig@gsi.de>
message:
Store correct random seed in parameter container

Between Root 6.22 and 6.24 the return value of TRandom3::GetSeed() was changed.
Since Root 6.24 the function GetSeed returns the current element of the state
used to generate the random number which returns a fixed value of 624 for
TRandom3.
To get the seed value which was set by the function SetSeed one neeeds to use
the GetSeed() function from the base class (gRandom->TRandom::GetSeed()),

FairSoft apr21p2 does not have the problem but any later FairSoft version will
save the wrong information in the parameter container FairBaseParSet
irrespective of the seed value defined in Root.
This commit fixes the issue and saves the correct seed value specified by
gRandom->SetSeed(<your value>).

message:
docs(doxygen): Declutter Sidebar (Modules)

The left sidebar of the Doxygen docs has a lot of entries.

A number of them are related to directories with only C++
code in them.  Many of them represent public/exported CMake
targets.

Doxygen has a structural element called "Modules" (in the
sidebar) to put those things under.  Modules can even have
submodules.  They can contain various C++ related elements
(classes, typedefs, enums, etc).

* Turn the README.md into README.dox, so that we get the full
  doxygen feature set.

* Put each of these as a module or submodule. (submodules
  have a \ingroup for the module.)

* No classes or other C++ entities have been moved into any
  modules yet.

deleted (if it is on the heap) as well.

So we need to delete our TTree before closing or
destructing the TFile.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Calm strncpy Warnings in MbsApi

strncpy() is a really bad API for copying strings over.
For example it always pads the destination with NUL bytes.
But does not NUL terminate in case of overflow.
See first stackoverflow link.

The nicest alternative to strncpy is strlcpy.  But that one
is not portable.  The second simplest one is using
snprintf().  Yes, this feels like overkill. But it's really
the by far most readable solution. So unless performance is
highly critical (in which case you shouldn't be using
strncpy anyway, as it pads!), snprintf should be fine.

Fixes: #1052
See: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2114896/why-are-strlcpy-and-strlcat-considered-insecure/2115015#2115015
See: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41869803/what-is-the-best-alternative-to-strncpy/41885173#41885173

author: Dennis Klein <d.klein@gsi.de>
message:
build: Workaround FindProtobuf lacking support for Protobuf >= 22

1. If we can find a Protobuf with a CMake pkg, we are good.
2. Otherwise fall back to FindProtobuf.
3. If we find Protobuf >= 22 and do not detect the missing `absl::`
   target (this is a guess that `absl::` targets will exist once
   FindProtobuf supports Protobuf >= 22), we set Protobuf as NOTFOUND.

Side notes:
Old CMake versions (< 3.27) see Protobuf >= 21 as major version 4.21+.

See also:
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v22.0
* https://protobuf.dev/news/2022-05-06/#versioning
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/12292
* https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/24847

cmake: Introduce fairroot_library_settings()

This is an internal function only.  It encapsulates things
that already happened and one new.

It is meant for all those libraries that get installed and
are expected to be used by other projects.
It is explicitly not meant for the examples. Because
they're not meant to be consumed by other projects.

Already happened:
* Add the FairRoot::${target} alias
* Set PROJECT_LIBRARY_PROPERTIES properties

New: fairroot_compile_features()

This sets cxx_std_* on the target.  This isn't very
granular, but hopefully fits the current development model
better.
The value being used depends on CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD or
PROJECT_MIN_CXX_STANDARD.
So when exported targets come, consumers will at least use
the CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD.

author: shahoian <ruben.shahoyan@cern.ch>
message:
Ask FairRunSim if TGeo should be imported to VMC

FairMCApplication.cxx unconditionally calls TVirtualMC::GetMC()->SetRootGeometry()
Materials/Media created via VMC are added both to TGeo and VMC geometry, so that
the importing the TGeo to VMC in the e.g. TGeant3TGeo::FinishGeometry() leads to
materials duplication and the loss of special (e.g. optical) properties set directly
on VMC materials 1st copy. This patch introduces a flag in the AliRunSim, which tells
to FairMCApplication if the TGeo should be imported to VMC. The flag is set to TRUE
in the constructor, therefore default behaviour of FairRoot is not altered. Those
applications which do not importing of TGeo (e.g. O2 always created the geometry
for the simulation on the fly) can set FairRunSim::SetImportTGeoToVMC(false)
BEFORE building the geometry

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Calm strncpy Warnings in MbsApi

strncpy() is a really bad API for copying strings over.
For example it always pads the destination with NUL bytes.
But does not NUL terminate in case of overflow.
See first stackoverflow link.

The nicest alternative to strncpy is strlcpy.  But that one
is not portable.  The second simplest one is using
snprintf().  Yes, this feels like overkill. But it's really
the by far most readable solution. So unless performance is
highly critical (in which case you shouldn't be using
strncpy anyway, as it pads!), snprintf should be fine.

Fixes: #1052
See: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2114896/why-are-strlcpy-and-strlcat-considered-insecure/2115015#2115015
See: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41869803/what-is-the-best-alternative-to-strncpy/41885173#41885173

Implemented fSource to FairRootManager with needed changes:

- FairSource: added few functions used in FairRootManager to get data from source:
    - GetObject - get any TObject from fSource
    - ActivateObject - to activate branch
    - CheckMaxEventNo - check number of events in the source, -1 by default/infinite
    - ReadBranchEvent - read only one branch, used by time-based reconstruction
    - FillEventHeader - fill event header information for the output file
- FairFileSource: added event headers, functions to generate event distribution
    - GetObject - temporary function to get needed object
    - ActivateObject - activate branch in the input tree/chain
    - CheckMaxEventNo - check the max event number
    - SetEventMeanTime, SetEventTimeInterval, SetBeamTime - functions to set event distribution function
    - SetEventTime, GetDeltaEventTime, GetEventTime - functions to set/get event time
    - ReadBranchEvent - to read only one branch from the tree
    - FillEventHeader - fill event header information for the output file
- FairMixedSource - similar to FairFileSource, but with mixed input
- FairRootManager - removed all functions to set file names, event distributions parameters, implemented one fSource only:
    - ReadEvent function now returns Int_t, 0 if all OK
- FairRunAna - input file setter functions, event distribution setter functions now point to specific implementations of fSource.
               The funcions are printing _obsolete warning_. Implemented two instances of FairSource: FairFileSource and FairMixedSource.
               The specific one is used dependently on the used setter function.
    - handler_ctrlc - implemented function to catch CTRL-C from the user to properly finish running and close the output file.

author: Dmytro Kresan <D.Kresan@gsi.de>
message:
Improve FairRunOnline. Cleanup of run managers.

1. Allow to use parameters in FairUnpackers.

Added SetParContainers() method to FairUnpack.
Separated method FairMbsSource::InitUnpackers().
Added source identification method.
Generate RunID if it was not set.

2. Unify data members of different run classes.

Use only one data member of FairEventHeader in the base class FairRun with needed getters and setters.
All derrived classes use this data member.

3. Create new class for online sources.

The last implementation assumed that all sources which need parameter containers in the unpackers are derrived
from FairMbsSource. This is not the case for many of the Sources used by CBM. Therefore an new class for online
sources was created which contain all the needed functionality. FairMbsSource is derrived from FairOnlineSource,
as well as the CBM specific source classes.

4. Avoid reading the first event in case of online source.

In case of online sources like lmd files or other raw data files the input file or input stream doesn't contain
an event header, so it doesn't make any sense to read the first event and try to extract one. The event header is
needed in case of ROOT files to extract the runID. The RunId for online files should be defined from the macro or
generated on the fly.

Be more Pedantic During Linking

On Linux, when creating a shared library, it is usually
allowed to have undefined symbols.
One reason, why this might be useful: A "main" program that
links to the library provides that symbol.

None of the shared libraries in FairRoot use this feature.
So let the linker enforce this.
Undefined symbols will now result in an error.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Drop check for "-std=*" in CXX_FLAGS

The old way of passing the wanted C++ language level into
FairRoot was to set (CMAKE_)CXX_FLAGS with a "-std=c++11"
flag.

In a more modern cmake world, one uses CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD
and target_compile_features() to let cmake choose the right
language level.
The problem starts here: cmake doesn't parse
CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS and so flags from both sources end up in
the final compile command.
If one wants to configure a project using the modern
methods, one does not want to use the old method.

This commit removes a fatal check, that enforces the user
to use the old method to set the language level.  That way
the user can choose the old or the modern way of doing it.

To be precise: This does not stop any current use. It only
removes some (old) "safety guards". And thus allows more
modern uses.

libraries.

   See the previous commit.

message:
Store correct random seed in parameter container

Between Root 6.22 and 6.24 the return value of TRandom3::GetSeed() was changed.
Since Root 6.24 the function GetSeed returns the current element of the state
used to generate the random number which returns a fixed value of 624 for
TRandom3.
To get the seed value which was set by the function SetSeed one neeeds to use
the GetSeed() function from the base class (gRandom->TRandom::GetSeed()),

FairSoft apr21p2 does not have the problem but any later FairSoft version will
save the wrong information in the parameter container FairBaseParSet
irrespective of the seed value defined in Root.
This commit fixes the issue and saves the correct seed value specified by
gRandom->SetSeed(<your value>).

(cherry picked from commit 20d04315fbd85c16ab39a05aaaacbfc75aadd10b)

message:
fix: Handle Sink/Source ownership more properly

FairRootManager and FairRun both used to `delete` fSink and
fSource. In specific situations (FairRootManager getting
destructed before FairRun) this leads to a double delete!

Deprecate the old FairRootManager::Set{Source,Sink} APIs
that take something like an owning pointer.

FairRootManager should only have a non-owning reference to
sink and source.  To allow FairRun to set it, `friend` it
from FairRootManager.

See: https://github.com/FairRootGroup/FairRoot/issues/1418
     (see "Double deleting of file source in
     FairRootManager and FairRun")

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Only Support Prepend in FairRootConfig.sh

Overriding PATH-like environment variables with information
at configure time requires users to re-add their local
directories after sourcing FairRootConfig.sh.

Appending has no good use case at all. It only adds a
fallback. This is normally not, what you want.

Which leaves us with prepend logic.

If your use case (say in your ExperimentRoot) requires
hardwiring PATH/etc, you can create
ExperimentRootConfig.sh, preset PATH/etc and inside that
script call FairRootConfig.sh.

It doesn't look like `set_env_macos.sh.in` is used inside
FairRoot at all. So drop it.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Calm strncpy Warnings in MbsApi

strncpy() is a really bad API for copying strings over.
For example it always pads the destination with NUL bytes.
But does not NUL terminate in case of overflow.
See first stackoverflow link.

The nicest alternative to strncpy is strlcpy.  But that one
is not portable.  The second simplest one is using
snprintf().  Yes, this feels like overkill. But it's really
the by far most readable solution. So unless performance is
highly critical (in which case you shouldn't be using
strncpy anyway, as it pads!), snprintf should be fine.

Fixes: #1052
See: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/2114896/why-are-strlcpy-and-strlcat-considered-insecure/2115015#2115015
See: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41869803/what-is-the-best-alternative-to-strncpy/41885173#41885173

author: Dennis Klein <d.klein@gsi.de>
message:
FairMQ: Parameterize the command interface initializing with sub socket

! THIS PATCH BREAKS NANOMSG TRANSPORT !

The subscriber command socket was created using the transport factory of
the channel which might not implement sub sockets. This patch creates
the subscriber command sockets in the device initialization and passes
them down (move) to the command interface initialization.

This patch puts more focus on the GetSocket interface of FairMQSocket,
because all command sockets are now implemented with the default
transport - the channels use an internal poller which polls over sockets
of potentially different transports now (e.g. zeromq command socket and
nanomsg data socket). Basically, all transports need to return file
descriptors compatible to be used in a single poll set. THIS IS NOT THE CASE!

! THIS PATCH BREAKS NANOMSG TRANSPORT !

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Drop check for "-std=*" in CXX_FLAGS

The old way of passing the wanted C++ language level into
FairRoot was to set (CMAKE_)CXX_FLAGS with a "-std=c++11"
flag.

In a more modern cmake world, one uses CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD
and target_compile_features() to let cmake choose the right
language level.
The problem starts here: cmake doesn't parse
CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS and so flags from both sources end up in
the final compile command.
If one wants to configure a project using the modern
methods, one does not want to use the old method.

This commit removes a fatal check, that enforces the user
to use the old method to set the language level.  That way
the user can choose the old or the modern way of doing it.

To be precise: This does not stop any current use. It only
removes some (old) "safety guards". And thus allows more
modern uses.

message:
build: Workaround FindProtobuf lacking support for Protobuf >= 22

1. If we can find a Protobuf with a CMake pkg, we are good.
2. Otherwise fall back to FindProtobuf.
3. If we find Protobuf >= 22 and do not detect the missing `absl::`
   target (this is a guess that `absl::` targets will exist once
   FindProtobuf supports Protobuf >= 22), we set Protobuf as NOTFOUND.

Side notes:
Old CMake versions (< 3.27) see Protobuf >= 21 as major version 4.21+.

See also:
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/releases/tag/v22.0
* https://protobuf.dev/news/2022-05-06/#versioning
* https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/12292
* https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/24847

author: Sebastien Binet <binet@cern.ch>
message:
examples/advanced: cmake support for go-examples

This CL adds basic support for compiling the Go-based examples.
Go is quite opinionated wrt a project layout.
It needs an environment variable $GOPATH (not unlike $PYTHONPATH)
pointing at a directory, under which a 'src' directory will hold all
the sources:
 $> cd $GOPATH
 $> ls
 src bin pkg
 $> tree -L 4 src
 src
 └── github.com
     ├── go-mangos
     │   └── mangos
     │       ├── AUTHORS
     │       ├── compat
     │       ├── conn.go
     │       ├── core.go
     │       ├── ...
     │       ├── util.go
     │       └── waiter.go
     └── sbinet-alice
         └── go-ex-sink-mq

This allows to have:
 $> go get github.com/sbinet-alice/go-ex-sink-mq

- fetch the sources from github.com/sbinet-alice/go-ex-sink-mq
- retrieve the dependencies of that program
  (github.com/go-mangos/mangos/...)
- compile all libraries under $GOPATH/pkg
- compile and install programs under $GOPATH/bin

To integrate with CMake:
- put the sources of go-processor and go-sink under
  `advanced/GoTutorial/src`
- make GOPATH point at advanced/GoTutorial
- use $GOBIN to make `go get` install the program(s) under that
  directory instead of $GOPATH/bin (which would be against CMake
  out-of-tree-build policy)

author: Radoslaw Karabowicz <r.karabowicz@gsi.de>
message:
Implemented fSource to FairRootManager with needed changes:

- FairSource: added few functions used in FairRootManager to get data from source:
    - GetObject - get any TObject from fSource
    - ActivateObject - to activate branch
    - CheckMaxEventNo - check number of events in the source, -1 by default/infinite
    - ReadBranchEvent - read only one branch, used by time-based reconstruction
    - FillEventHeader - fill event header information for the output file
- FairFileSource: added event headers, functions to generate event distribution
    - GetObject - temporary function to get needed object
    - ActivateObject - activate branch in the input tree/chain
    - CheckMaxEventNo - check the max event number
    - SetEventMeanTime, SetEventTimeInterval, SetBeamTime - functions to set event distribution function
    - SetEventTime, GetDeltaEventTime, GetEventTime - functions to set/get event time
    - ReadBranchEvent - to read only one branch from the tree
    - FillEventHeader - fill event header information for the output file
- FairMixedSource - similar to FairFileSource, but with mixed input
- FairRootManager - removed all functions to set file names, event distributions parameters, implemented one fSource only:
    - ReadEvent function now returns Int_t, 0 if all OK
- FairRunAna - input file setter functions, event distribution setter functions now point to specific implementations of fSource.
               The funcions are printing _obsolete warning_. Implemented two instances of FairSource: FairFileSource and FairMixedSource.
               The specific one is used dependently on the used setter function.
    - handler_ctrlc - implemented function to catch CTRL-C from the user to properly finish running and close the output file.
    - removed RunMixed() function as well as all differences between standard and mixed running
    - checking for changed RunId is done via FillEventHeader function
- FairRunAnaProof - removed reference to fMixedInput
- FairRunOnline - fSource is now in the mother class, FairRunAna; plus some minor changes

	base/source/FairFileSource.cxx
	base/source/FairFileSource.h

message:
docs(doxygen): Declutter Sidebar (Modules)

The left sidebar of the Doxygen docs has a lot of entries.

A number of them are related to directories with only C++
code in them.  Many of them represent public/exported CMake
targets.

Doxygen has a structural element called "Modules" (in the
sidebar) to put those things under.  Modules can even have
submodules.  They can contain various C++ related elements
(classes, typedefs, enums, etc).

* Turn the README.md into README.dox, so that we get the full
  doxygen feature set.

* Put each of these as a module or submodule. (submodules
  have a \ingroup for the module.)

* No classes or other C++ entities have been moved into any
  modules yet.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Improve CXX_STANDARD Detection

First for users of FairRoot:
* FairRoot exports the `CXX_STANDARD` level as
  `FairRoot_CXX_STANDARD`.
* `Check_Compiler()` uses this to set the minimum
  `CXX_STANDARD` for any users of FairRoot.  You should
  call `Check_Compiler()` after `find_package(FairRoot)`.

For FairRoot itself:
* If `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD` is not set from outside, detect
  ROOT's `CXX_STANDARD` from its
  `target_compile_features()`.  This means, that
  `Check_Compiler()` must be called after
  `find_package(ROOT)`.
* If `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD` is not set, try to ask
  fairsoft-config.
* Handle `PROJECT_MIN_CXX_STANDARD`.

author: Dmytro Kresan <D.Kresan@gsi.de>
message:
Improve FairRunOnline. Cleanup of run managers.

1. Allow to use parameters in FairUnpackers.

Added SetParContainers() method to FairUnpack.
Add ReInit() to the Unpacker class.
Move SetParContainers for unpackers to base FairSource class.
Separated method FairMbsSource::InitUnpackers().
Avoid dynamic cast in FairRunOnline.
Call SetParUnpackers, InitUpackers, and ReInitUnpackers from FairRunOnline.
Added source identification method.
Set the run ID using source.
Generate RunID if it was not set.
Call fSource->Close() in the Finish method of FairRunOnline.

2. Unify data members of different run classes.

Use only one data member of FairEventHeader in the base class FairRun with needed getters and setters.
All derrived classes use this data member.

3. Create new class for online sources.

The last implementation assumed that all sources which need parameter containers in the unpackers are derrived
from FairMbsSource. This is not the case for many of the Sources used by CBM. Therefore an new class for online
sources was created which contain all the needed functionality. FairMbsSource is derrived from FairOnlineSource,
as well as the CBM specific source classes.

4. Avoid reading the first event in case of online source.

In case of online sources like lmd files or other raw data files the input file or input stream doesn't contain
an event header, so it doesn't make any sense to read the first event and try to extract one. The event header is
needed in case of ROOT files to extract the runID. The RunId for online files should be defined from the macro or
generated on the fly.

5. Fix linking error with Xcode 7.3.

6. Add possibility to skip writing an event to tree.

7. Allow to change the name of the output tree.

Read the name of the output tree from VMCWORKDIR/config/rootmanager.dat.
If no file is present the default name is cbmsim.
Add instructions on how to change treename to main README.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Drop check for "-std=*" in CXX_FLAGS

The old way of passing the wanted C++ language level into
FairRoot was to set (CMAKE_)CXX_FLAGS with a "-std=c++11"
flag.

In a more modern cmake world, one uses CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD
and target_compile_features() to let cmake choose the right
language level.
The problem starts here: cmake doesn't parse
CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS and so flags from both sources end up in
the final compile command.
If one wants to configure a project using the modern
methods, one does not want to use the old method.

This commit removes a fatal check, that enforces the user
to use the old method to set the language level.  That way
the user can choose the old or the modern way of doing it.

To be precise: This does not stop any current use. It only
removes some (old) "safety guards". And thus allows more
modern uses.

author: Florian Uhlig <f.uhlig@gsi.de>
message:
Store correct random seed in parameter container

Between Root 6.22 and 6.24 the return value of TRandom3::GetSeed() was changed.
Since Root 6.24 the function GetSeed returns the current element of the state
used to generate the random number which returns a fixed value of 624 for
TRandom3.
To get the seed value which was set by the function SetSeed one neeeds to use
the GetSeed() function from the base class (gRandom->TRandom::GetSeed()),

FairSoft apr21p2 does not have the problem but any later FairSoft version will
save the wrong information in the parameter container FairBaseParSet
irrespective of the seed value defined in Root.
This commit fixes the issue and saves the correct seed value specified by
gRandom->SetSeed(<your value>).

(cherry picked from commit 20d04315fbd85c16ab39a05aaaacbfc75aadd10b)

author: Dmytro Kresan <D.Kresan@gsi.de>
message:
Improve FairRunOnline. Cleanup of run managers.

1. Allow to use parameters in FairUnpackers.

Added SetParContainers() method to FairUnpack.
Separated method FairMbsSource::InitUnpackers().
Added source identification method.
Generate RunID if it was not set.

2. Unify data members of different run classes.

Use only one data member of FairEventHeader in the base class FairRun with needed getters and setters.
All derrived classes use this data member.

3. Create new class for online sources.

The last implementation assumed that all sources which need parameter containers in the unpackers are derrived
from FairMbsSource. This is not the case for many of the Sources used by CBM. Therefore an new class for online
sources was created which contain all the needed functionality. FairMbsSource is derrived from FairOnlineSource,
as well as the CBM specific source classes.

4. Avoid reading the first event in case of online source.

In case of online sources like lmd files or other raw data files the input file or input stream doesn't contain
an event header, so it doesn't make any sense to read the first event and try to extract one. The event header is
needed in case of ROOT files to extract the runID. The RunId for online files should be defined from the macro or
generated on the fly.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Improve Include Paths in Generated Dictionaries

General notes:

- We do not want source or build directory names in the
  generated dictionaries. Those paths might not exist after
  installing, or might contain other content (worse: it
  could be malicious content).

- dictionaries have an "include path list" which gets
  appended to ROOT's include search list at loading of the
  dictionary. This list should have sensible entries.

So:

- Add the final install include dir to the include search
  path of generated dictionaries.

  Note: It looks like extracting the install include paths
  from a target is a nontrivial task in CMake. So we need
  to explicitly pass it in.

- It is generally a better idea to pass non-absolute header
  paths to rootcling.  It sometimes stores the given path
  in the dictionary.

  Preferably this should be the relative path used in
  `#include` statements.
  So do not make those paths absolute.

- Strip build directory entries from the generated
  dictionaries include path list.

  Source directory entries should also be stripped, but the
  test suite seems to fail.  So let's keep it for now.

- Deduplicate the include path list.

author: Dmytro Kresan <D.Kresan@gsi.de>
message:
Improve FairRunOnline. Cleanup of run managers.

1. Allow to use parameters in FairUnpackers.

Added SetParContainers() method to FairUnpack.
Add ReInit() to the Unpacker class.
Move SetParContainers for unpackers to base FairSource class.
Separated method FairMbsSource::InitUnpackers().
Avoid dynamic cast in FairRunOnline.
Call SetParUnpackers, InitUpackers, and ReInitUnpackers from FairRunOnline.
Added source identification method.
Set the run ID using source.
Generate RunID if it was not set.
Call fSource->Close() in the Finish method of FairRunOnline.

2. Implement new functions which are defined in FairSource base class to existing sources.

3. Unify data members of different run classes.

Use only one data member of FairEventHeader in the base class FairRun with needed getters and setters.
All derrived classes use this data member.

4. Create new class for online sources.

The last implementation assumed that all sources which need parameter containers in the unpackers are derrived
from FairMbsSource. This is not the case for many of the Sources used by CBM. Therefore an new class for online
sources was created which contain all the needed functionality. FairMbsSource is derrived from FairOnlineSource,
as well as the CBM specific source classes.

5. Avoid reading the first event in case of online source.

In case of online sources like lmd files or other raw data files the input file or input stream doesn't contain
an event header, so it doesn't make any sense to read the first event and try to extract one. The event header is
needed in case of ROOT files to extract the runID. The RunId for online files should be defined from the macro or
generated on the fly.

6. Fix linking error with Xcode 7.3.

7. Add possibility to skip writing an event to tree.

message:
cmake: Introduce fairroot_library_settings()

This is an internal function only.  It encapsulates things
that already happened and one new.

It is meant for all those libraries that get installed and
are expected to be used by other projects.
It is explicitly not meant for the examples. Because
they're not meant to be consumed by other projects.

Already happened:
* Add the FairRoot::${target} alias
* Set PROJECT_LIBRARY_PROPERTIES properties

New: fairroot_compile_features()

This sets cxx_std_* on the target.  This isn't very
granular, but hopefully fits the current development model
better.
The value being used depends on CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD or
PROJECT_MIN_CXX_STANDARD.
So when exported targets come, consumers will at least use
the CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Use WriteTObject instead of cd + Write

Instead of
```c++
tfile->cd();
tobj->Write();
```
one can also do
```c++
tfile->WriteTObject(tobj);
```

This has the advantage that it does not modify the global
gDirectory/gFile (which the calling code might want to keep).

Also fix some small memory leaks.

See-Also: https://root.cern/root/htmldoc/guides/users-guide/InputOutput.html#saving-objects-to-disk

author: Florian Uhlig <f.uhlig@gsi.de>
message:
Major update of Tutorial4.

Fix memory problem.
Add possibility to store information about coordinate system.
Allow to save MCPoints in local or global coordinates.
Stop execution of hit producer when MCPoints are in global coordinates.
Fix errors in eventdisplay macro.
New draw class to draw MCPoints in local and global coordinates correctly.

Fix a double free when deleting the TGeoManager. This memory problem only occured when reverting the misalignment.
The problem had to do with the way the physical nodes have been treated when undoing the misaligment.

Add a data member to the parameter container which allows to store the information if the MCPoints are in the local
or the global coordinate system. The default value is kFALSE which mean that the MCPoints are stored in the local
coordinate system. Previous data was always stored in the local coordinate system. With the default value the old
data should be interpreted correctly. Fixes #119 @2h.

Add the possibility to chosse between MCPoints in global or local coordinates. Add function to set this from the macro.
Store the information about the coordinate system in FairTutorialDet4GeoPar parameter container. The default value is
to use local coordinates which was the default also before the change. In case the geometry is modified the values
are stored in local coordinates even if the default was changed to global coordinates. Print warning when switching
the coordinate system. Fixes #118 @1h.

Since the hit producer can only work with MCPoints in local coordinates stop the execution when MCPoints are in
global coordinates. Add and use parameter container which contain the information about the coordinate system.
Refs #117 @1h.

Add return type for eventdisplay function which is needed when using ROOT6.
Change name of MCPoint branch. Otherwise the MCPoints could not be read.

Add a new class which draws the MCPoints for the eventdisplay. The class can work with MCPoints stored in
global or local coordinate system. In case the MCPoints are in local coordinates the positions are transformed
to the global coordinate system.
Fixes #120 @1.5h.

Create also a seperate geometry file which contains the misaligned geometry. The call is done from the macro.
Misalign one of the detector stations of Tutorial4 by 10cm to be cleary seen in the geometry viewer and the
event display.

author: Sandro Wenzel <sandro.wenzel@cern.ch>
message:
Ability to register/retrieve data of any type with IO manager

This commit provides a major extension to the FairRootManager, enabling
the user to register branches based on arbitrary types.
In particular, it is now possible to register stl containers as branch
entries, extending the current TObject* or TCollection* APIs.

Instant cratification:
```
// some source registering data
auto ioman = FairRootManager::Instance();
std::vector<CustomData>* data;
ioman->RegisterAny("mybranch", data, ...);
```

```
// some consumer task asking for the data
auto ioman = FairRootManager::Instance();
auto mydata = ioman->InitObjectAs<std::vector<CustomData> const*>("mybranch");
```

The example "simulation/Tutorial2" was extended accordingly showing use cases
with persistent and non-persistent branches.

The IO to ROOT trees works as before. It was checked that splitting of branches
based on std::vectors still works the same way as for TClonesArrays.

The user has to create dictionaries for any entry she wants to put into
a persistent branch.

Further notes:
  a) the new mechanism does not use folders; Hence the persistent branches
     have to be created explictly (done in FairMCApplication for the moment)
  b) the commit is incompletely in many ways; It demonstrates correct working
     for a simple FileSource
  c) Existing API is fully preserved. The user can use the traditional API as well
     as the new API at the same time.
  d) The new API imposes that input data obtained from InitObjectAs is unmodifiable
     (a const view on data)

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
fix(cmake): Handle Double CMake in Using Projects

A typical "ExperimentRoot" project uses FairRoot by using
its find-Module (by adding the right path) and calling
find_package(FairRoot).

This setup worked for the first call to CMake (configure
step), but reconfiguring (running CMake again) did not
work correctly.

Add tests for this (that fail without this fix).

The find module recursively calls find_package(FairRoot
CONFIG) to load the new config mode package.
This sets FairRoot_DIR to the directory containing the
config mode package. This variable is a cache variable and
persists into the next run of CMake.

The old find module used to think, that FairRoot_DIR could
be the prefix of the FairRoot installation.

Rewrite:

* Use FAIRROOTPATH and ENV{FAIRROOTPATH} only to extend
  CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH to search the config mode package
* Use FairRoot_PREFIX from the config mode package to guide
  further old style detection
* Use FindPackageHandleStandardArgs

message:
Remove unneeded if when deleting NULL / 0 / nullptr

C++ standard dictates that NULL / 0 / nullptr is a valid argument for
delete which then simply has no effect:

"The value of the first argument supplied to a deallocation function may
be a null pointer value; if so, and if the deallocation function is one
supplied in the standard library, the call has no effect."

I therefore think in these particular case it's safe to remove the ifs.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Only Support Prepend in FairRootConfig.sh

Overriding PATH-like environment variables with information
at configure time requires users to re-add their local
directories after sourcing FairRootConfig.sh.

Appending has no good use case at all. It only adds a
fallback. This is normally not, what you want.

Which leaves us with prepend logic.

If your use case (say in your ExperimentRoot) requires
hardwiring PATH/etc, you can create
ExperimentRootConfig.sh, preset PATH/etc and inside that
script call FairRootConfig.sh.

It doesn't look like `set_env_macos.sh.in` is used inside
FairRoot at all. So drop it.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
ci(warnings): Do not Ignore Failed Builds

When looking for a reference build to compare a new build
to also include failed builds.

* Builds for which the clang-tidy run itself fails
  (compiler error, etc) do not get recorded at all, because
  the recordIssues step isn't started at all (fail fast,
  basically).
* So failed builds are due to build failures in other areas
  (broken build machine, compiler error on other
  compilers).
* So taking a "failed" (due to other things) build as a
  reference is okay, because we compare one successful run
  on the clang-tidy "platform" to another successful run.

pixelSimSplit is the implementation of the MC simulation in MQ, where
generated events are sent to transport devices:

- FairMQPrimaryGeneratorDevice - generates events and sends them (in whole or in chunks);
- FairMQTransportDevices - receives generated events (or chunks of them) and transports them in G3 or G4;
- FairMQChunkMerger - merges chunks of individual events into full events;
- FairGenericStack/FairStack - added new function SetParticleArray();
- FairMQRunDevice - base class for FairMQSimDevice.

Generatoror and transporter may work in push-pull or reply-request mode.

Two tests available, in pure MQ and in DDS.
