author: Radoslaw Karabowicz <r.karabowicz@gsi.de>
message:
FastSimulation.

Implemented feature allows user to move transported particles
in TGeant3 or TGeant4 to any position.
It is used when implementing fast simulation in some detector
to move particle forward out of this detector to reduce computing time.

Introduced methods of the FairGenericStack should be implemened
by individual experiments, as shown in FairStack:
FastSimMoveParticleTo(): moves the particle to a position and momentum specified by the user.
FastSimStopParticle(): kill the current particle.
FastSimGetMovedIndex(): to get the stack index of the moved particle.
FastSimClearMovedIndex(): to clear the index (set it to -2).

base/sim/fastsim develops a fast simulation model for Geant4 that uses
TG4VUserFastSimulation to implement the functionality.

author: Alexey Rybalchenko <alexryba@gmail.com>
message:
Several FairMQ fixes and improvements:

- FairMQ: add possibility to poll on multiple channels.
- FairMQ: include command channel when polling on blocking calls (for unblocking without termination).
- FairMQ: move signal handler inside of FairMQDevice class (call FairMQDevice::CatchSignals() in the main function).
- FairMQ: add 'bool CheckCurrentState(statename)' (instead of 'GetCurrentState() == statename' that cannot be thread safe).
- FairMQDevice: add 'InteractiveStateLoop()' method that can be used to change states from the command line.
- FairMQDevice: add automatic transition to IDLE state if Run() exits without an external event.
- FairMQDevice: implement device reset.
- FairMQDevice: use unordered_map for device channels.
- FairMQChannel: improve address validation for channels.
- FairMQChannel: add ExpectsAnotherPart() method to check if another msg part is expected (old approach still works).
- FairMQ: remove invalid transition from the run files.
- FairMQFileSink: disable ROOT termination signal handler.
- Tutorial3: spawn xterm windows from start scripts without overlapping for better visibility.
- FairMQ Examples: update protobuf test and move its files to a common directory.
- FairMQStateMachine: improve feedback on invalid transitions (more readable).

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Tutorial3: Use Fixtures Instead of Depends

In CMake tests `DEPENDS` is only asking for proper
ordering. That is "A depends on B" only means that B runs
before A, but nothing more.

if A should only start if B was successful, one needs
fixtures.  B will declare a "setup fixture" and A then
lists this fixture as required.

defined. The alias is local because CMake resolves it during target export. This means

depending on yaml-cpp.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Improve Include Paths in Generated Dictionaries

General notes:

- We do not want source or build directory names in the
  generated dictionaries. Those paths might not exist after
  installing, or might contain other content (worse: it
  could be malicious content).

- dictionaries have an "include path list" which gets
  appended to ROOT's include search list at loading of the
  dictionary. This list should have sensible entries.

So:

- Add the final install include dir to the include search
  path of generated dictionaries.

  Note: It looks like extracting the install include paths
  from a target is a nontrivial task in CMake. So we need
  to explicitly pass it in.

- It is generally a better idea to pass non-absolute header
  paths to rootcling.  It sometimes stores the given path
  in the dictionary.

  Preferably this should be the relative path used in
  `#include` statements.
  So do not make those paths absolute.

- Strip build directory entries from the generated
  dictionaries include path list.

  Source directory entries should also be stripped, but the
  test suite seems to fail.  So let's keep it for now.

- Deduplicate the include path list.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Drop check for "-std=*" in CXX_FLAGS

The old way of passing the wanted C++ language level into
FairRoot was to set (CMAKE_)CXX_FLAGS with a "-std=c++11"
flag.

In a more modern cmake world, one uses CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD
and target_compile_features() to let cmake choose the right
language level.
The problem starts here: cmake doesn't parse
CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS and so flags from both sources end up in
the final compile command.
If one wants to configure a project using the modern
methods, one does not want to use the old method.

This commit removes a fatal check, that enforces the user
to use the old method to set the language level.  That way
the user can choose the old or the modern way of doing it.

To be precise: This does not stop any current use. It only
removes some (old) "safety guards". And thus allows more
modern uses.

author: Sandro Wenzel <sandro.wenzel@cern.ch>
message:
Add consistency check/warning in FairMCApplication::ConstructGeometry

The FairMCApplication::ConstructGeometry assumes that the geometry volumes
are fully instantiated after calling the ConstructGeometry function on each detector modules.

This might not be the case, for instance when users are using TVirtualMC::Gsvol interface with
negative parameters which get fixed only later (during the closing phase of the geometry).
In consequence, all lookup tables might be incomplete or inconsistent.

This commit provides the following:

 * Issue a warning when ConstructGeometry was actually incomplete

 * Checking if gGeoManager is available at beginning of function

 * Fixing a size problem in a for-loop used for the index to module mapping

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
ci(warnings): Do not Ignore Failed Builds

When looking for a reference build to compare a new build
to also include failed builds.

* Builds for which the clang-tidy run itself fails
  (compiler error, etc) do not get recorded at all, because
  the recordIssues step isn't started at all (fail fast,
  basically).
* So failed builds are due to build failures in other areas
  (broken build machine, compiler error on other
  compilers).
* So taking a "failed" (due to other things) build as a
  reference is okay, because we compare one successful run
  on the clang-tidy "platform" to another successful run.

was misused to remove the `TFolder` from `gROOT`

This folder is no longer removed in the sink's `WriteFolder()`.

Introduced a new `FairRootManager::RemoveOutputFolderForMtMode()` function
which removes the `TFolder` from `gROOT`, which is needed in the
MT mode in TGeant4 transport.
Used this function in `FairMCApplicaiton::InitGeometry()`
and in `FairMCApplication::InitFinalizer()`.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
ci(warnings): Do not Ignore Failed Builds

When looking for a reference build to compare a new build
to also include failed builds.

* Builds for which the clang-tidy run itself fails
  (compiler error, etc) do not get recorded at all, because
  the recordIssues step isn't started at all (fail fast,
  basically).
* So failed builds are due to build failures in other areas
  (broken build machine, compiler error on other
  compilers).
* So taking a "failed" (due to other things) build as a
  reference is okay, because we compare one successful run
  on the clang-tidy "platform" to another successful run.

message:
FairRun: Now Owns the FairSource

FairRunAna and FairRunOnline both had a SetSource method.
Both used to just call SetSource on FairRootManager.
Move this into FairRun.

FairRootManager deletes the source in its destructor. As
FairRootManager is a singleton, this happens very late in
the process lifetime. Too late for some ROOT interpreter
use cases.
So move the ownership to FairRun.
FairRun makes sure that FairRootManager does not have a
pointer to delete.

author: Sandro Wenzel <sandro.wenzel@cern.ch>
message:
Ability to register/retrieve data of any type with IO manager

This commit provides a major extension to the FairRootManager, enabling
the user to register branches based on arbitrary types.
In particular, it is now possible to register stl containers as branch
entries, extending the current TObject* or TCollection* APIs.

Instant cratification:
```
// some source registering data
auto ioman = FairRootManager::Instance();
std::vector<CustomData>* data;
ioman->RegisterAny("mybranch", data, ...);
```

```
// some consumer task asking for the data
auto ioman = FairRootManager::Instance();
auto mydata = ioman->InitObjectAs<std::vector<CustomData> const*>("mybranch");
```

The example "simulation/Tutorial2" was extended accordingly showing use cases
with persistent and non-persistent branches.

The IO to ROOT trees works as before. It was checked that splitting of branches
based on std::vectors still works the same way as for TClonesArrays.

The user has to create dictionaries for any entry she wants to put into
a persistent branch.

Further notes:
  a) the new mechanism does not use folders; Hence the persistent branches
     have to be created explictly (done in FairMCApplication for the moment)
  b) the commit is incompletely in many ways; It demonstrates correct working
     for a simple FileSource
  c) Existing API is fully preserved. The user can use the traditional API as well
     as the new API at the same time.
  d) The new API imposes that input data obtained from InitObjectAs is unmodifiable
     (a const view on data)

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Improve Include Paths in Generated Dictionaries

General notes:

- We do not want source or build directory names in the
  generated dictionaries. Those paths might not exist after
  installing, or might contain other content (worse: it
  could be malicious content).

- dictionaries have an "include path list" which gets
  appended to ROOT's include search list at loading of the
  dictionary. This list should have sensible entries.

So:

- Add the final install include dir to the include search
  path of generated dictionaries.

  Note: It looks like extracting the install include paths
  from a target is a nontrivial task in CMake. So we need
  to explicitly pass it in.

- It is generally a better idea to pass non-absolute header
  paths to rootcling.  It sometimes stores the given path
  in the dictionary.

  Preferably this should be the relative path used in
  `#include` statements.
  So do not make those paths absolute.

- Strip build directory entries from the generated
  dictionaries include path list.

  Source directory entries should also be stripped, but the
  test suite seems to fail.  So let's keep it for now.

- Deduplicate the include path list.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Be more Pedantic During Linking

On Linux, when creating a shared library, it is usually
allowed to have undefined symbols.
One reason, why this might be useful: A "main" program that
links to the library provides that symbol.

None of the shared libraries in FairRoot use this feature.
So let the linker enforce this.
Undefined symbols will now result in an error.

author: Christian Tacke <58549698+ChristianTackeGSI@users.noreply.github.com>
message:
Only Support Prepend in FairRootConfig.sh

Overriding PATH-like environment variables with information
at configure time requires users to re-add their local
directories after sourcing FairRootConfig.sh.

Appending has no good use case at all. It only adds a
fallback. This is normally not, what you want.

Which leaves us with prepend logic.

If your use case (say in your ExperimentRoot) requires
hardwiring PATH/etc, you can create
ExperimentRootConfig.sh, preset PATH/etc and inside that
script call FairRootConfig.sh.

It doesn't look like `set_env_macos.sh.in` is used inside
FairRoot at all. So drop it.

See-Also: ef405a5c5c6514db05c552134a71267f6f8177ab

message:
Improved NXdata behavior

Creating an NXdata group now adds ‘signal’ and ‘axes’ attributes to the
group attributes. A rename operation on the signal will update these
attributes. Also, when creating an NXdata group with signal and axes of
the same ‘nxname’ , the signal gets renamed. This prevents problems
when the signal NXfield is created by an operation on an axis NXfield
that returns an NXfield with the same ‘nxname’, e.g., NXdata(np.sin(x),
x), where x is an NXfield - in this case, the signal ‘nxname’ is set to
‘signal’.

author: Ray Osborn <rayosborn@mac.com>
message:
Various enhancements to tree.py

1) Refactored data value reads, with new NXFile._readvalue and
NXFile.open functions, to facilitate subclassing of NXFile for remote
file access. Core memory files are now opened directly in h5py, instead
of through NXFile, so that they are not affected by the lack of
persistence of NXFile file handles.
2) Added a parent attribute to AttrDict to allow attributes to be
written directly to HDF5 files, if the file mode allows it.m Also added
__delitem__ to AttrDict and __delattr__ to NXfield to allow deletion of
attributes.
3) Improved efficiency of h5py file updating. Before this, whole groups
would be rewritten if a single field was added to it.
4) Customized NXlink.update so that links are automatically updated.
Otherwise, NXfield.update would call NXFile._writedata which just
returns the link info without performing an update.

author: Matthias Vogelgesang <matthias.vogelgesang@kit.edu>
message:
Fix loading libNeXus.so under Ubuntu 12.04

The libnexus package of Ubuntu (and probably Debian) does not install a symbolic
link under /usr/lib/libNeXus.so to /usr/lib/libNeXus.so.0, hence loading fails.
This is not a fault by the distributions but related to the way loading is done
in Nexpy.

I fixed the problem using find_library of the ctypes.util module, which
automatically searches for a library under all major platforms. I highly suggest
to replace the hand-written code with that, making loading a) cleaner and b)
more reliable.

author: Ray Osborn <rayosborn@mac.com>
message:
Prevent closure of dialogs when pressing the Enter key

Users often press the Return or Enter keys after editing text boxes.
This is often interpreted as triggering the default dialog box button,
i.e., ‘OK’ or ‘Save’, which then closes the whole dialog. This catches
these two key presses and posts a Tab key press event instead. The
dialog can only be closed by clicking on the relevant button.

author: rpavlick <ryan.pavlick@gmail.com>
message: Adding rcurve.py containing several functions that compute the radii of curvature for an ellipsoid. Adding rsphere.py containing several functions that compute the radii of auxiliary spheres. Adding latitude.py containing several functions that compute auxiliary latitudes and their inverse functions. Adding 'loxodrome_direct' to compute the end point of a loxodromic curve from a start lat/lon, azimuth, and distance. Fixing 'loxodrome_inverse', it previously failed on the degenerate case of east/west azimuth. Adding 'meanm' which computes the geographic mean of points on a spheroid. Adding 'departure' which computes the distance between two longitudes at a specified latitude. Adding 'meridianarc' which computes the distance between two latitudes along a specified longitude. Added thirdflattening and eccentricty attributes to ellipsoid definitions. Removed all instances '%%' in comments.

Add two functions to new module `pymap3d/spherical.py`:
`geodetic2spherical` and `spherical2geodetic` to convert between
geocentric geodetic (latitude, longitude, altitude) and geocentric
spherical coordinates (spherical latitude, longitude, radius).

latitude=45 with values pre-computed from the implementation in Boule.
Add the functions to the API definition in `pymap3d/__init__.py` and to
the list of functions in the `README.md`.

message:
Merge branch 'master' of https://github.com/rpavlick/pymap3d

* 'master' of https://github.com/rpavlick/pymap3d:
  Adding rcurve.py containing several functions that compute the radii of curvature for an ellipsoid. Adding rsphere.py containing several functions that compute the radii of auxiliary spheres. Adding latitude.py containing several functions that compute auxiliary latitudes and their inverse functions. Adding 'loxodrome_direct' to compute the end point of a loxodromic curve from a start lat/lon, azimuth, and distance. Fixing 'loxodrome_inverse', it previously failed on the degenerate case of east/west azimuth. Adding 'meanm' which computes the geographic mean of points on a spheroid. Adding 'departure' which computes the distance between two longitudes at a specified latitude. Adding 'meridianarc' which computes the distance between two latitudes along a specified longitude. Added thirdflattening and eccentricty attributes to ellipsoid definitions. Removed all instances '%%' in comments.

that would have succeeded. Previously, this used the same fallback value for all
positions if even just one failed.

author: benoit <jambonkapa@jaaayyymail.com>
message:
Bugfix for ecef2geodetic on pole edge cases.

Explaination: on poles, ecef2geodetic does some tan(angle+eps), with
angle possibly close to pi/2 (or -pi/2). With float conversions,
angle+eps might be cast to float32 which does not work well with the
tan() discontinuities.

Illustration:
>>> print(pymap3d.ecef2geodetic(*np.array([[0,0,1]], dtype=np.float64).T, deg=1))
(array([-89.99999], dtype=float32), array([0.], dtype=float32), array([-6356751.5], dtype=float32))
>>> math.tan(np.float32(np.pi/2))
-22877332.42885646
>>> np.float32(np.pi/2) > np.pi/2
True

Fix logic: fix the latitude when we are on these edge cases.
These edge cases are identified using the float precision of the
parameters used.

Test modification: Using half the semiaxis for altitude change instead
of a single meter to not have test failures due to precision issues.

message: Adding rcurve.py containing several functions that compute the radii of curvature for an ellipsoid. Adding rsphere.py containing several functions that compute the radii of auxiliary spheres. Adding latitude.py containing several functions that compute auxiliary latitudes and their inverse functions. Adding 'loxodrome_direct' to compute the end point of a loxodromic curve from a start lat/lon, azimuth, and distance. Fixing 'loxodrome_inverse', it previously failed on the degenerate case of east/west azimuth. Adding 'meanm' which computes the geographic mean of points on a spheroid. Adding 'departure' which computes the distance between two longitudes at a specified latitude. Adding 'meridianarc' which computes the distance between two latitudes along a specified longitude. Added thirdflattening and eccentricty attributes to ellipsoid definitions. Removed all instances '%%' in comments.

The language tags for several languages were updated using the IANA registry with relevant subtags (e.g. chinese pinyin --> pny):
https://www.iana.org/assignments/language-subtag-registry/language-subtag-registry
For languages written in latin alphabet the w3 rules on script subtags were used:
https://www.w3.org/International/articles/language-tags/#script
https://www.iso.org/schema/isosts/v1.0/doc/n-cvd0.html
